evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: This call will just take around ten to fifteen minutes. Is now a good time? [framing present with time box, yes received, but 'quote you can depend on' language missing and not explicitly promised before probing starts]
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: And I'd like to ask first what are your biggest concerns and what are the most important things you want answers to on this call today? [asked before probing; customer replies with 'Just costs really' — only one concern raised]
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Nicole acknowledges 'I see, no worries. We can definitely talk about your move' but does not ask 'tell me more about that' or probe deeper into cost concern; immediately pivots to logistics probing instead
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: No summary reflection offered. Nicole responds to customer's cost concern with acknowledgment only ('I see, no worries'), not a structured 'So what I'm hearing is X, Y, Z' reflection
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Property type (one-story house) ✓, floor/stories ✓, storage container dimensions ✓, box count ~25-30 ✓, furniture list ✓, driveway/parking ✓; missing walking distance and clear additional rooms count for the destination house. Partial coverage
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Never offered; rep does not ask about packing service
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Approximately how many boxes? [asked and answered: 25-30 boxes plus 3 totes]
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: It usually takes around four to five hours... I will estimate this to take around five to six hours... It's good to budget around $1,220 to $1,426. [Anchor given with typical range, and later re-anchored at $911 to $1,117 when customer clarifies smaller load. Both personalized to customer's specific route (one-hour drive) and load detail.]
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: We charge $206 per hour... $190 travel fee... no hidden fees of any type, no credit card fees, no Stero fees, no disassemble or reassembly fees... we have a minimum of two and a half hours once we go over the minimum the time is prorated in fifteen minute increments. [Full fee transparency and 2.5-hour minimum + 15-minute increment framing delivered]
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Rep does not ask 'Does that feel fair?' after the revised estimate. Customer volunteers concern instead: 'I don't know so I wanted to, I wanted to clarify a couple of things'
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: if we cannot make it in the time window that we arrange, we immediately start discounting money of your final bill... the time start as soon as we get on site and open the contract [Discount terms stated clearly]
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: we have no worries, damage coverage. We provide up to $2,000 per move to repair, replace or reimburse for any accidental damages. [Amount and purpose stated, but missing explicit 'no deductible' and 'no fine print' framing, and does not clearly state it's built into the rate, not an add-on]
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: Rep does not ask 'Does that put those to rest?' or equivalent; call ends abruptly when customer requests email due to doctor's appointment
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Never asked. Customer says 'if it's gonna be between $12 and $1,400 it's just not something that we can afford' but rep does not follow up with 'What's still concerning you?' before pivoting to item list. Call ends without a final concerns check
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Would you like me to get you on the schedule? [Weak softened ask with immediate out: customer says 'I don't know so I wanted to clarify a couple of things' and then later requests email. No hard close attempted; rep accommodates without re-asking]
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: To secure a spot, there's no deposit required if you have to reschedule or cancel, no fees for that either. [Rate lock / no-deposit concept mentioned]
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: No booking confirmed. Customer defers to email and call ends without date, phone, arrival window, crew size, or next-step confirmation.

top_strength: Nicole handled a complex, multi-stop logistics scenario (pod storage, long-distance drive, item inventory clarification) with patience and accurately re-estimated the move in real time when the customer clarified the actual load size, reducing the quote from $1,220–$1,426 to $911–$1,117.
coaching_note: After re-anchoring the estimate, ask 'Does that feel fair?' and pause for a real response before accepting the customer's deferral to email — and when the customer cites affordability as a concern, ask 'What's still concerning you?' with a genuine follow-up rather than letting the call drift toward 'send me the quote' without confirming next steps or asking for the business.
